The Corp's report carries a full discussion of these various proposed measures and a copy of same can be furnished upon request.
With particular importance to this study, is the most obvious alternative; to protect the area from future flooding is that of building a wall and/or levee system along the east bank of the River. The relative disadvantages of the proposal (known as Scheme C) are discussed in the Corp's statement on this matter.
That statement from the Copies published impact strdy reads as follows:
Scheme C - North Harrisburg
"Scheme C was investigated as a plan to protect the northern part of Harrisburg and a portion of Susquehanna Township in the Lucknow area from Susquehanna River flooding. This Scheme consists of a concrete wall along Front Street from Forster Street at the Taylor Bridge, north to Miller's Lane in the Lucknow area. From this point an earth levee would extend eastward to high ground. Other items included in this Scheme are six pumping stations along the wall to transfer internal drainage to the River, storm drain piping and intercept chambers, a closure structure at the point where the levee crosses U.S. Route 322 in the Lucknow Area, and a special closure structure at the Walnut Street Bridge. The structures included in this Scheme would prevent River-flood damage to Harrisburg from north of Capital to Lucknow. However, the total first costs are extremely high, ranging from $20 million for the 100- year flood $28.5 million for the flood of record, the 1972 Flood. Moreover, the annual costs outweigh the expected annual benefits by a ratio of more than five to one. These economic factors, coupled with the environmental disadvantage of a five-mile-long wall which would block the view of the River, caused this Scheme to be eliminated from consideration."
The above alternatives cannot be considered a complete alternative for the project since they would only reduce the likelyhood of flooding in the area. They could reduce the needs for some of the flood plain conservation measures, i.e., acquisition, clearance, reuse. The measures cannot be considered as alternatives for project activities that are involved with the restoration of the area.
